results.description: An airline's fuel consumption per available seat mile (ASM), a measure of fuel efficiency.
An airline's total profit divided by its total Available Seat Miles (ASM), measuring profitability per unit of capacity.
The average age in years of an airline's fleet, indicating operational efficiency and future capital expenditure needs.
The growth rate in the total value of a homebuilder's backlog, representing homes under contract but not yet delivered.
The one-year change in a bank's Modified Texas Ratio, a measure of credit stress comparing non-performing assets to tangible equity and loan loss reserves.
A bank's total assets adjusted for their associated credit risk, used in determining regulatory capital requirements.
The percentage of a bank's total deposits that are held in savings and money market accounts, indicating deposit base stability.
A bank's core equity capital as a percentage of its total risk-weighted assets; a primary measure of financial strength.
The three-year change in a bank's ratio of total expenses to average assets, a measure of long-term efficiency trends.
The one-year growth rate in the number of a telecommunications company's broadband internet subscribers.
The period-over-period change in the market capitalization implied by a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation model.
A valuation momentum metric representing the change in the ratio of free cash flow to market capitalization over a period.
The period-over-period change in the ratio of a company's free cash flow to its total assets.
The one-year growth in revenue recognized from ongoing construction projects, relevant for engineering and construction firms.
A mining industry metric representing the estimated number of years a mine can operate based on its current proven reserves and production rate.
The change in the consensus analyst expectation for the future development and revision of an energy company's reserves.
The growth rate in the number of a company's operational facilities, such as stores, branches, or plants.
The period-over-period change in a company's free cash flow on a per-share basis.
A valuation ratio comparing a company's trailing twelve-month free cash flow to its market capitalization, synonymous with free cash flow yield.
A company's earnings per share (EPS) from its primary business operations, adjusted to exclude non-recurring or unusual items.
The market capitalization of a company as implied by a fundamental Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation model.
The one-year growth in a company's profit, calculated using a proprietary unweighted fundamental methodology.
For Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), the ratio of operating income to interest expense, measuring the ability to service debt.
The proportion of earnings retained in the business rather than paid out as dividends, calculated as 1 minus the dividend payout ratio.
The gross profit margin for companies primarily engaged in the homebuilding industry.
The growth rate in the total number of surgeries performed by a hospital or healthcare provider.
The one-year growth in revenue generated from house sales, a key top-line growth metric for homebuilders.
The one-year growth rate of the consensus net profit estimate for a given industry.
An insurance company's ratio of incurred claims and loss adjustment expenses to earned premiums.
A measure of an insurer's underwriting profitability, calculated as the sum of incurred losses and expenses divided by earned premiums.
An insurance industry efficiency metric calculated by dividing underwriting and acquisition expenses by net premiums written.
An insurer's ratio of net premiums written to its net assets, measuring leverage and underwriting risk.
An insurance metric representing the profitability of underwriting activities, calculated as underwriting income divided by premiums earned.
The growth rate in the number of licensed beds for a hospital operator, indicating capacity expansion or reduction.
A financial ratio comparing a bank's loan loss provisions to its total equity reserves, gauging its buffer against potential loan defaults.
A ratio measuring the amount of new oil and gas reserves a company adds to its portfolio relative to the amount it extracts.
The growth in a company's oil and gas reserves on a per-share basis, indicating changes in asset value attributable to each share.
The change in the total cost associated with an energy company's oil and gas reserves.
The one-year change in the number of patient admissions for a hospital or healthcare provider.
The one-year change in a bank's ratio of non-accruing loans to total assets, serving as an indicator of changing asset quality.
The one-year growth in a homebuilder's ratio of housing revenue to total investment, indicating changing capital efficiency.
The one-year growth rate in the number of new patent applications filed by a company, a leading indicator of R&D activity.
For healthcare firms, the one-year growth in the number of drug candidates in Phase 3 clinical trials, a key pipeline indicator.
The one-year growth in Revenue Per Customer (or Client), a key unit economic metric in industries like telecom or software.
The one-year growth rate in the number of wireless subscribers for a telecommunications company.
A key airline industry cost metric, also known as CASM, that measures operating expenses per unit of passenger carrying capacity.
An airline metric representing the percentage of available seating capacity that has been filled with paying passengers.
The one-year growth rate in the number of patents held by a company, indicating the pace of innovation.
A valuation metric representing the ratio of a company's total number of patents to its market capitalization.
A technical or model-based signal representing the residual component of a stock's price from a valuation model, normalized by market capitalization.
A valuation ratio for financial institutions that compares the stock price to its pre-provision net revenue (PPNR) on a per-share basis.
The growth rate of a company's physical production output, such as barrels of oil equivalent for energy firms or ounces of metal for mining firms.
A valuation ratio for energy or mining companies comparing physical production volume (e.g., barrels of oil) to market capitalization.
An energy sector valuation metric that represents the ratio of an energy company's proved oil and gas reserves to its market capitalization.
A measure of the return generated from capital spent on acquiring new energy reserves.
A metric for resource companies (energy, mining) indicating the rate at which reserves are being depleted, typically production divided by total reserves.
The change in the rate at which an energy company's proved reserves are being depleted, indicating the sustainability of its production levels.
The growth rate of an energy company's proved reserves, indicating its ability to replace production.
The change in an energy company's proved reserves scaled by its market capitalization, indicating the value of reserve changes.
The one-year growth in an airline's total miles traveled by paying passengers (RPM), a key measure of air traffic demand.
The one-year growth rate in the net number of subscribers added by a telecommunications company.
A banking performance metric measuring the three-year change in operating income normalized by the bank's core Tier 1 equity capital.
The one-year growth rate of a company's total investments as reported on its balance sheet.
The average total revenue generated per operational facility, often used for healthcare, retail, or REITs.
The percentage of a telecom company's target market that has subscribed to its wireless services.
